item.title: GTA 6 Features Weird Al and Janelle James on the Radio and Original Music From The Weeknd
item.description:
GTA 6 has celebrity radio hosts and original music in Leonida, with credits to many artists, including Weird Al Yankovic and Lana Del Rey. Find out all the hosts and artists that players can hear while cruising through Vice City.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Features 22 Music Stations and Two Talk Stations


Star-Studded Radio Hosts Include Lana Del Rey, Bad Bunny, and Weird Al Yankovic


Pictured: Kodak Black at the Jack of Hearts strip club.
Grand Theft Auto 6's radio lineup brings together a star-studded cast of real-life musicians, actors, and comedians across 22 music stations and two talk stations, with several celebrities also helping write the material players hear. Rockstar’s official credits confirm the following music-station hosts, including presenters of shows within those stations, with some of them even posting on their socials about the extent of their involvement.
In Rockstar’s official credits, the studio's GTA TV & Radio section credits DJ Pooh and Joey Henson as the writing directors, alongside several senior and associate writers. The studio also credited a few of these hosts who helped with additional writing, namely Weird Al Yankovic, Doug Stanhope, Brian Posehn, Janelle James, and Stavros Halkias. In his Bluesky post, legendary parody artist Yankovic confirmed he helped write some of the in-game commercials and voices the Burger Shot ads, in addition to hosting Vice City FM.
  • AfroBank FM: Burna Boy as Burna and Jay Donaldson (Palms Trax) as Palmsy.
  • Back Country Radio: Morgan Wallen as MW, Lana Del Rey as Delta Dawne, and Jeremy Dufrene as roving reporter Mud Dog Mike.
  • CircoLoco Records Radio: Seth Troxler as DJ Seth and Antonio Carbonaro as DJ Antonio.
  • Cocoteo FM: Bad Bunny as El Martillo and RaiNao as La Gata.
  • Dirty South Classics: Trina and Trick Daddy as themselves, with Gucci Mane appearing as himself while hosting The Tap In.
  • Emotion 98.3: Doug Stanhope as Doug Van Dyke.
  • Flash FM: Robyn and Alex Consani as themselves.
  • Gloriana Blues Radio: Buddy Guy as DJ Buddy and Keith Richards as DJ Keith.
  • Honey FM: Chilli and T-Boz as themselves, with Craig Robinson as Liquid Wilson, hosting Liquid City.
  • Kaleidoscope FM: Jeremy Irons as DJ Dicky.
  • Leonida Jazz Radio: Randy Brecker as DJ Randy and Stanley Clarke as DJ Stanley, with Yussef Dayes appearing as himself while hosting The Nook.
  • Radio La Ola: Gloria Estefan as Gloria and Emilio Estefan as Emilio.
  • Radio On-U: Adrian Sherwood as himself.
  • Stockyard FM: The Dare as Harrison and PinkPantheress as Victoria.
  • Symphony FM: Yuja Wang as Yuja.
  • The Chamber 106.6: Kerry King as DJ Kerry, Tom Araya as DJ Tom, and Brian Posehn as Big Fan Brian.
  • The Vault Radio: DJ Pretzel as himself.
  • Vice City FM: Weird Al Yankovic as DJ Al and Brigitte Nielsen as Madame Brigitte.
  • Vice City Rap Radio: JT as DJ JT and DJ Stevie J as DJ Stevie, with Charlamagne tha God as Charlamagne and Ivy Rivera as Ivy, hosting Early AF.
  • V-Rock: Lindsey Buckingham as The Buck and Michael McDonald as Skipper McD.
  • Worldwide FM: Gilles Peterson as himself.

Kodak Black also hosts the separately credited program The Sniper of La Perle, presented by Michaël Brun. This hidden, unlockable radio station primarily features Haitian music and requires the player to scan four posters around the map.
Craig Robinson also helped create the music for Liquid City, the Honey FM show he hosts as Liquid Wilson. Rockstar’s credits list eight original songs for the show, with Robinson sharing songwriting credits on six of them.

Wipe and WKTT Provide Absurd Social Commentary


The Wipe and WKTT make up the game’s two talk-radio stations, following a more conversational style with GTA’s signature unhinged and satirical humor. Abbot Elementary star Janelle James voices Tish on She Got Assets for The Wipe, an opportunity she said she pursued with Rockstar. She also conceptualized, pitched, and scripted the show, adding that she’s been playing the game since Vice City.
  • The Wipe — Ask Dr. Nita: Anitta as Dr. Nita.
  • The Wipe — El Otro Lado: John Leguizamo as Enrique "El Enigma" Romero.
  • The Wipe — She Got Assets: Janelle James as Tish.
  • WKTT — The Richard Bastion Show: Jason Sudeikis as Richard Bastion.
  • WKTT — Hit the Bricks: Stavros Halkias as Dominic "The Brick" Brizzolato

GTA 6’s Original Score Brings Together Justice, The Weeknd, Djo and More


Rockstar Says Original Music Plays a Big Part for Jason and Lucia's Story


Rockstar partnered with Atlantic Records on Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, a collection of 34 new recordings featuring artists including Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa, Travis Scott, Cardi B, and JENNIE. Before launch, ten songs were released for streaming, but the whole album and even a separate vinyl release are available to purchase.
Alongside that album, French duo Justice composed GTA 6’s original score. Before launch, players could hear "Flower in a Hurricane," featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard. At the time of writing, it has over 23 million views on YouTube, with the community hailing it as the game's theme song. Moreover, "Pusher," featuring Gesaffelstein, and "Starting From Zero," featuring Michael McDonald, also appear in the score and on the 34-track companion album.
Rockstar’s launch credits confirmed two further Justice collaborations with "My Only Vice," featuring The Weeknd, and "The Night’s Coming," featuring Djo. During a Q&A with Rockstar, we confirmed that it was an original track composed for the game. "Original music is a huge part of Grand Theft Auto’s identity, and it plays a big part throughout Jason and Lucia’s story," Rockstar said.
Music and radio have always been a huge part of GTA, giving each city its own sound and personality. Even as Rockstar rethinks familiar elements like sex workers and casual encounters, GTA 6’s celebrity radio hosts and original music keep that vibe going. Players can now drive around to Leonida's radio as GTA is out for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with a PC release coming in the future, check out our review below:

item.title: GTA 6 Cuts Sex Partners, Prostitutes, and Other Longtime Features, Rockstar Explains Why
item.description:
GTA 6 leaves out a classic open-world feature to solicit adult services, a feature dating back to GTA 3. Find out Rockstar's explanation for their choice and the initial fan reaction.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Leaves Some Longtime Series Traditions Behind


GTA 6 Drops the Ability to Solicit Adult Services


In Grand Theft Auto 6, players can no longer solicit prostitutes, ending a series tradition that’s been around since GTA 3. As fans and early reviews have documented, this feature isn’t in the launch version, and there’s currently no similar mechanic in the game.
In a Q&A with Rockstar, we asked if Jason and Lucia can have intimate relationships or sleep with others outside their partnership. Rockstar Vice President of Design Stephen Donkin didn’t give a direct answer. Instead, he talked about the overall design philosophy for GTA 6 and why some familiar features were left out.
"GTA 6 is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run," Donkin said. "While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in 6 has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon." He pointed out that Rockstar focused on improving the radio, wanted system, robberies, and car theft.
Donkin also said that "many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTA 6," since the studio focused on features that fit Jason and Lucia’s story. He didn’t list which features were removed, but in a separate interview with Kotaku, he confirmed that players can’t gamble at Leonida’s casinos, explaining that gambling didn’t fit the story and could upset the in-game economy.

Some GTA 6 Fans Want the Freedom to Make Jason Cheat on Lucia


Many longtime fans are unhappy with the change and have shared their frustrations on social media. Some question why Jason and Lucia’s relationship should limit these activities, since past GTA protagonists had more freedom to act outside the main story. In the previous title, players noted that GTA 5 let Michael solicit prostitutes even though he was married to Amanda.
Some fans have been more direct, saying they want the option to have Jason cheat on Lucia. Players have discussed whether infidelity could affect the couple’s relationship or change the story’s outcome. Others hoped the game would allow them to pursue other romantic interests like Mandy, a popular early-game side character who flirts with Jason and is suggested to be violent and possibly a serial killer.

Jason and Lucia’s Romance Is Supposed to Be Optional


Player Choice Only Goes So Far in GTA 6


Jason and Lucia will spend much of GTA 6 working together regardless of how close they become. In a September interview with Famitsu, Rockstar North Head of Development and Co-Studio Head Rob Nelson made clear that the romance itself is optional, saying, "whether they go through those situations together as a couple or simply as accomplices is up to the player."
The effort players put into the relationship affects what Jason and Lucia can do together, as Nelson told Famitsu that if players ignore the romance, they lose affectionate actions like holding hands and kissing, but investing in the relationship brings them back.
Players who aren’t interested in romance can still finish the story with Jason and Lucia as partners in crime. Still, fans have pointed out that these statements contrast with the removal of these nightlife activities, as it takes away one of the ways players could previously make choices outside a protagonist’s established relationship.
GTA 6 still offers players a lot of freedom, but Rockstar is setting clearer limits on the story. In keeping Jason and Lucia’s relationship the core of the story, the game had to sacrifice some of its older open-world freedoms that, historically, didn’t affect the main narrative. For more on the game, check out our review below:

item.title: GTA 6 Launch Is Official Leave and Party Day For Several Studios, Brands and Even an Army Unit
item.description:
GTA 6 launched on November 19, and companies from Palworld’s Pocketpair to Logitech marked it with official leave, livestreams and office parties. Here is how the industry celebrated and what it shows about GTA’s pull today.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Launch Reshaped Work Schedules Worldwide


Launch Day Arrived With Cleared Calendars


When Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) went live at midnight on November 19, a wave of companies had already cleared their calendars for it. Some handed employees official leave to play, and others threw parties at the office. Many workers around the world simply requested the day off.
GTA 6 is the first numbered entry in Rockstar Games’ crime series in 13 years. Rockstar announced the November 19, 2026 date after an earlier delay from May. The game unlocked at midnight local time on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The rollout began at midnight in New Zealand and moved across time zones from Tokyo to Miami, which brought launch parties and some companies giving staff the day off.

Employers Saw the Absences Coming


The planning started well before launch week. Payroll processor Gusto reported that paid time off requests for launch day were up 9% compared with the two prior weeks. BambooHR data put requests for November 19 at 9% to 17% above a typical third Thursday in November, and a BambooHR spokesperson noted that a broader trend toward using paid time off more freely could also play a part. These figures cover requests, so they describe plans and leave actual attendance unmeasured.

Gaming Companies Granted Official Leave for the Launch


Pocketpair Gave Players on Staff Five Days Off


The most generous policy came from the developer of Palworld. Pocketpair announced on November 12 that it would grant staff special leave from November 19 through November 23, sharing an image of the internal notice on the official Palworld X account. The company framed the break as “an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City.” The notice added that “such a historic occasion deserves our full attention,” excused staff who planned to play from regular duties, and covered a weekend, so it used three leave days.
Leadership joined in. CEO Takuro Mizobe wrote that he would be “taking a break for a while to play GTA6 too.” Palworld and Craftopia updates were set to continue on schedule during the break.

Logitech Turned the Launch Into a Company-Wide Game Day


Logitech took a wider approach with “Logi Game Day.” Every employee, interns included, can take one day off to play a game of their choice, and the initiative is the first company-wide gaming day in Logitech’s history.
The company backed the policy with a stated rationale. CEO Hanneke Faber said, “It’s time to retire the stereotype that gaming is a waste of time.” Chief people officer Elaine Laird added, “Play is not the opposite of work.” Logitech G general manager Robin Piispanen said Game Day “gives our team a shared purpose.”

Bulkhead and Other Businesses Scheduled Their Own Breaks


Bulkhead, the studio behind the tactical shooter Wardogs, set its break for the weeks right after launch. CEO Joe Brammer told Edge magazine the whole team would take December off following the game’s early access launch. The stated reason is rest after the early access launch and Season 2. Bulkhead pulled Season 3 content forward to November 12, a week before GTA 6 arrived.
Brammer’s advice to players covered the rest of the month: “Go play GTA 6, we need to detox.” The line shows how comfortable a studio can be with a release of this size sitting next to its own game.
Businesses outside gaming made similar moves. California-based Burger Motorsports suspended operations for the launch, citing employee scheduling conflicts, and planned to resume once staff had completed at least one mission. Fox29 reported that a US Army battalion at Fort Stewart offered a four-day pass to soldiers who reenlisted. In India, boAt offered an optional day off.

Launch Parties Marked the Release in Offices and Cities


Pocketpair, Logitech G and Fans Held Launch Events


Leave policies gave way to celebrations once the game went live. Reuters photographed Pocketpair employees playing GTA 6 at the company’s Tokyo office, and reported that the company threw a sushi party to celebrate the launch. The office party matched the tone of the original notice, which treated the release as a shared occasion for the whole team.
Logitech G scheduled a livestream from its San Jose headquarters on November 19, with general manager Robin Piispanen, a former competitive gamer, set to host.
Outside company walls, retail venues and gaming bars hosted their own events. A launch party at Grails Miami marked the midnight release on November 18, and players gathered at Bamboo Gaming Center & Bar in Bangkok on launch day. Together with the studio events, they showed that GTA 6 drew crowds in person as well as online.

GTA 6 Is the Most Influential Release in Gaming Right Now


Sales Estimates and Studio Reactions Show GTA 6’s Reach


The commercial picture is still forming. Sensor Tower estimated cumulative digital sales of $1.84 billion by release day, more than double the $800 million GTA V made in its first 24 hours. These are third-party estimates, and Take-Two has not shared pre-order data. Take-Two’s own numbers will be the ones to watch.
Take-Two’s leadership kept its focus on the present. During a TBPN interview on launch day, CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked about a future Grand Theft Auto and replied that GTA 6 had only just gone live. The exchange shows how quickly attention moves to what comes next.
Reactions from rival studios point the same way. Pocketpair named the game in its leave notice, Bulkhead pointed its audience toward it, and Logitech tied its first Game Day to it. 80.lv also reported that other studios moved their own releases away from the launch window. The calendar now bends around a single date, and that is rare for any entertainment product.

Our Take: Official Leave Replaced the Sick Day


Our reading of the launch is that employers formalized what many workers were already planning. The companies above gave employees official time in advance, and Logitech’s release tied gaming to confidence and work performance. The practice also gives HR teams a template for the next release that moves millions of people at once.
GTA 6 now sets the schedule for work, for rival studios and for conversations about workplace culture. Whether the leave trend outlasts launch week is a question for the coming months.

item.title: GTA 6 Censored in Japan, Says No to Naked Jason and Tones Down Gore
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI features censored nudity and toned-down gore in its Japanese release compared to other regions. Read on to learn more about Jason showering in underwear, the blood and gore changes, and fan reactions.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Japan Release Alters Nudity and Tones Down Gore


Nudity Changes Leave Jason in Underwear During Shower Scenes


Grand Theft Auto VI has rolled out with noticeable regional edits in Japan, where players have found that nudity is covered up or altered compared to the international release. While players in other regions see full nudity in certain moments across the open world, the Japanese version keeps characters covered up even in private scenes.
The most talked-about detail among players is that Jason wears underwear rather than appearing nude during shower scenes, with similar clothing adjustments applied to other characters and NPCs. Some explicit scenes and beach or shower moments have either had extra clothing added or been cut back entirely, prompting disappointment from fans in Japan who noticed the difference right after launch.
Players also picked up on early hints before launch when store listings showed the Japanese download sitting roughly 1 GB smaller than the standard global build, coming in at around 208.73 GB on PS5 and 208.74 GB on Xbox Series X|S compared to roughly 209.91 GB and 209.86 GB elsewhere, alongside a CERO Z rating that lacked a sexual content icon. Many fans online pointed out how jarring it feels to have an adult rating while still seeing underwear during routine moments like taking a shower.

Blood, Gore, and Other Differences in the Japanese Version


Nudity is not the only area scaled back in Japan, as coverage from Japanese outlet Game Spark and player reports also highlighted differences in how blood and gore are handled visually. In the Japanese release, the option to adjust blood and gore intensity is missing, leaving less blood overall compared to versions in other regions.
Even with reduced blood effects and dismemberment adjustments, players noted an odd contrast where extreme violence like shooting someone's head off can still happen while nudity remains covered up. Meanwhile, other parts of the game such as strip clubs and drug use still appear in the world, showing how selective the regional adjustments are across Leonida.
For players looking to see everything from Grand Theft Auto 6 without regional cuts, the difference in Japan has become a major talking point right at launch.

GTA 6 Japan Fans Left Frustrated by Censorship


Clips and screenshots showing Jason taking a shower in black underwear quickly circulated online, sparking debate among players comparing the Japanese build with the uncensored release elsewhere. In other regions, Jason appears completely unclothed in the shower, making the added trunks stand out to fans paying close attention to regional differences.
Many players in Japan questioned why such strict edits were applied when public bathhouses and hot springs are a familiar part of their everyday culture, while others wondered why a game already carrying a strict 18+ age rating classification still needed nudity covered up. Across social media like Twitter/X, several commenters expressed frustration over feeling like they were getting a tamer version of a title that is already built around gritty adult themes.
To know more about our thoughts on Grand Theft Auto 6, check out our review below:

item.title: GTA 6 Is Making It Really Hard to Actually Commit Grand Theft Auto
item.description:
GTA 6 has ditched the classic one-button carjacking system in favor of specialized tools, mini-games, and GPS trackers. Read to learn how players can steal parked cars in the game and what fans think about the new carjacking mechanics.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Pushes For More Realism in Carjacking


Stealing Cars is Harder Than Ever Before


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) makes stealing cars far more challenging than in previous titles, leaning into a more realistic criminal experience. For nearly three decades, the core loop of GTA has been dead simple: walk up to any vehicle on the street, tap a single button, and speed off. With the release of GTA 6, however, Rockstar Games has overhauled that signature formula, making the franchise’s namesake crime significantly harder to pull off.
As Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained in preview interviews ahead of launch, the studio wanted to move away from binary, one-button vehicle thefts. Instead, GTA 6 introduces a tiered vehicle security system where the difficulty of stealing a parked car depends entirely on its value and era.
Older models only require a Slim Jim and a hotwiring mini-game, while modern and luxury cars demand an unlockable digital key cloner. Even after boosting a high-end ride, players must disable its alarm and built-in GPS tracker to keep police from tracking their location. To know more about GTA 6’s new carjacking mechanics, check out our article on GTA 6 How to Steal Cars.
Of course, players can still bypass parked-car security by carjacking vehicles with drivers already behind the wheel, though doing so immediately draws witnesses and police attention in Vice City's denser, tighter streets. Combined with new fuel management mechanics and punishingly realistic driving controls—especially when trying to use your phone behind the wheel—GTA 6 turns what used to be an effortless reflex into a calculated risk.

Fans Divided on the New Car Stealing Mechanics


The new carjacking mechanics drew immediate online pushback, with players expressing concern that leaning too heavily into hyperrealism could detract from the chaotic, mindless fun GTA is known for. Fans across X (Twitter) and Reddit pointed out that stopping to complete tedious break-in mini-games on parked cars disrupts the momentum of intense shootouts and police escapes.
GTA 6 also blocks players from stealing cars near Jason and Lucia’s safehouses and specific story hubs, a restriction some fans feel undercuts the signature freedom of the franchise. However, others in the community defended the rule, arguing that boosting cars on your own turf is a terrible idea in real life anyway.
Regardless, GTA 6 continues to dominate the whole gaming community since it launched, sparking multiple discussions about the game leaving out sex partners, prostitutes, and other longtime features. To know more about our thoughts on Grand Theft Auto VI, check out our review below.
Sources:
GTA 6 The Big Interview
r/GTA6unmoderated | i like the fact that you can’t steal a car in your neighborhood. have some empathy.

item.title: GTA 6 Hidden Red Dead Easter Eggs All But Confirm Rockstar’s Shared Universe Theory
item.description:
GTA 6 hides even more Easter eggs linking it to Red Dead Redemption. Here’s what players have uncovered so far, and where fans stand on the shared-universe theory.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Adds Fuel to Red Dead Redemption Connection Fan Theory


Arthur Morgan’s Cowboy Hat and More RDR Easter Eggs


For over a decade, Rockstar Games fans have debated one of gaming’s biggest lore mysteries: do Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption share the same universe? While Rockstar has historically treated nods between the two franchises as playful winks rather than hard canon, GTA 6 is making that stance much harder to maintain with all the RDR Easter eggs and references.
One of which is a cowboy hat that resembles RDR2’s Arthur Morgan’s own. While the game doesn't explicitly say the headwear belongs to the iconic outlaw, the “Genuine Cowboy Hat” features a rope band similar to what Arthur wore. Players can get the hat for as low as $5 at a yard sale located on Orchard Avenue, South of Port Gellhorn.
GTA 6 also scatters copies of a Western novel across the map about a cowboy in New Austin, the iconic frontier region from Red Dead Redemption. On top of that, players have spotted paper bills featuring portraits of RDR2’s Thaddeus Waxman and President Hardin, suggesting that both titles share the same timeline.
While not strictly an Easter egg, fans have also pointed out Jason Duval’s uncanny resemblance to Arthur Morgan. Months before GTA 6 launched, players theorized Jason could be Arthur’s descendant based on their shared jawline, build, and rugged Southern demeanor. That theory gained even more traction at launch, as fans noticed the two also share a similar drawl, deadpan delivery, and reluctant-outlaw attitude.

A Split in the Theory


The GTA x RDR same-universe theory first began when GTA 5 launched in 2013. It sparked after players spotted a book titled Red Dead by "J. Marston" on Franklin’s bookshelf and found John Marston as a heritage option in GTA Online.
Rockstar fueled the theory with GTA Online treasure hunts for RDR2 weapons, "vanderlinde" emails, and RDR2’s time-traveler Francis Sinclair, whose birthmark links him to GTA V’s Epsilon Program. However, despite the latest Easter eggs found in GTA 6, some fans remain unconvinced that GTA and RDR share the same timeline.
Most of the skepticism stems from geographical contradictions, namely that Red Dead references real-world locations like New York and California. In contrast, GTA uses fictionalized counterparts like Liberty City and San Andreas.
Rockstar Games has neither confirmed nor denied these theories, and as players continue exploring Vice City, fans may uncover even more clues linking GTA and RDR. To know more about our thoughts on Grand Theft Auto 6, check out our review below.

item.title: GTA 6 Sells Over 24 Million Copies and Hits 120 Million Hours Worth of Views on Launch Day
item.description:
GTA 6 is estimated to have sold millions of copies on launch day, while livestreams of the game set viewership records across Twitch, Kick, and YouTube. Read on to learn more about the milestones from GTA’s official release.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

Grand Theft Auto VI: Launch Breaks Sales and Streaming Records


GTA 6 Hits Record Sales and Streaming Numbers in Its First 24 Hours


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) has kicked off its launch with estimates that the game sold roughly 24.6 million copies and brought in about $2.36 billion through launch day on November 19, while Twitch, Kick, and YouTube all saw record-setting of over 120 million hours worth of views within that timeframe.
On a platform that estimates and records analytics and data, Sensor Tower's range covers the full launch day, and these numbers also include pre-orders. A reading taken earlier the same day put the game at already 19.1 million units and $1.84 billion, so the total climbed by more than five million copies over the course of the day. Figures vary slightly depending on the report, ranging from 24.58 to 24.59 million units, but all-in-all still land around the 24.6 million mark.
For comparison, GTA 5 previously earned roughly $800 million on its first day in 2013, which makes GTA 6's estimate nearly three times higher. If the estimate holds, that would also make it the biggest video game launch to date.
According to the reported breakdown, around three in four copies were sold on PlayStation 5, at about 18.44 million units and $1.77 billion, compared with roughly 6.15 million units and $588 million earned on the Xbox Series X|S. For disclaimer, these are still third-party estimates as Rockstar and Take-Two have not announced official launch-day sales, though Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has reportedly said official data will be shared soon.

GTA 6 Livestreams Set Records Across Multiple Platforms


Streams Charts reports that GTA 6 drew 125.47 million hours watched across tracked platforms in its first 24 hours, with a combined peak of 7.91 million concurrent viewers. This amount is more than 4.5 times the previous launch record held by VALORANT, which had reached 1.74 million viewers.
PlatformHours WatchedPeak Viewers
Twitch52.3 million3.31 million
YouTube44 million3.22 million
Kick27.8 million1.5 million

On Twitch, that peak makes GTA 6 the most-watched game ever on the platform, passing the record League of Legends set at its 2022 World Championship final. It also set the record for the most hours watched by a single game in one day on both Twitch and Kick, and ranks second among games on YouTube, at this time of writing.
Among individual streamers, IShowSpeed led for hours watched with 4.47 million, followed by TheBurntPeanut with 3.89 million and alanzoka with 3.11 million. Meanwhile, IlloJuan recorded the highest peak, at 562,000 viewers.

Players Impressed With GTA 6's Record Start


Reactions to the GTA’s achievements upon release leaned toward awe, with players calling the launch "unreal" and some having played the game non-stop since. Several pointed out that the totals and sales would have been even larger if it had launched or was available on PC. Even so, the current numbers from platforms alone make it a standout accomplishment.
GTA 6 launched Thursday, November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, priced at $79.99 for the Standard Edition and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition. A PC port has not been announced at this time. To know more about our thoughts and insights on Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), check out our review below:

item.title: GTA 6's Hyperrealism Makes the Lack of Controversial Features Stand Out More
item.description:
13 years of chasing action RPG perfection produced a world as absurdly real as its inspirations. But cut features create a jarring loss of agency for some in a world as lived-in as Leonida, even after some reports turned out to be ragebait.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

Rockstar Tried to Strike a Balance Between Realism and Playability


For over a decade, Rockstar continually fell behind schedule in pursuit of polish and perfection. Glowing reviews suggest that GTA 6 has lived up to everyone's high expectations, delivering hyperrealistic gameplay with heart.
But cutting controversial features for narrative focus, playability, or other reasons only makes the resulting lack of realism more obvious in a world as close to real life as Leonida. And as it turns out, some reported missing features were actually ragebait hoaxes that ended up burying actual controversial omissions.
Life in GTA 6’s fictional Florida, Leonida, is made remarkably lifelike by the mundane need to eat, shower, and sleep, and NPCs that Rockstar gave "a singular awareness" to, according to GTA 6’s Development Notes. Among other features like a prone stance, grocery shopping was cut from the game to achieve a balance between realism and playability, Rockstar North Co-Studio Head Rob Nelson told Famitsu in an August 2026 interview.
Even so, the mechanics they retained still dive deeper into life-simulation than past Rockstar games. Players now have to watch personal stats like how many calories Jason and Lucia eat and how much daily exercise they get. They must actively maintain the protagonists' relationship through consistent communication and quality time. Even grand theft auto is harder than ever before.
"Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief," The Guardian writes. This attention to detail has earned the game critical acclaim for its realism, but based on online discussions, it also makes the less realistic aspects even more jarring. After all, if you can control the way Lucia opens a door, then why can’t you pull out a gun whenever you want?

The Real Missing ‘Controversial’ Features


Following GTA 6's November 19 release, which required a whopping 212GB of pre-load, players took to the internet to share their first impressions. Initially praised for its writing and realism, complaints about the game eventually trickled in, chief among them being that Jason can't physically cheat on Lucia. Not with fan-favorite bombshell Mandy, and not even with prostitutes.
Although players can still pay for a dance at a strip club—to the detriment of Jason and Lucia's relationship, if they go alone—this is the first time in 25 years that Rockstar has completely removed the option to hire prostitutes.
We talked about how the omission of this feature affects gameplay in our review, and asked Rockstar about the reasoning behind the controversial change. VP of Design Stephen Donkin told us that "everything we have implemented in 6 has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon."
The option to dual-wield weapons, absent since San Andreas but present in Max Payne 3 and Red Dead Redemption 2, was also left out in favor of a more grounded combat system that also limits weapon inventory to two handguns and two long guns. And a functional stock exchange system, as seen in GTA 5’s LCN and BAWSAQ markets, is notably missing.
Players are no longer able to replay missions, as well. Rockstar has not released an official statement as to why mission replay was removed from GTA 6. But the decision makes sense considering the game’s branching story, which has “more than two” possible endings, according to our Q&A with the studio.
Some players argue that taking away any player choice goes completely against the indulgent open-world concept GTA is known for, especially in the series’ most hyperrealistic entry yet, and that the game’s steep price tag should entail total freedom. However, others say that the game’s design makes sense with its narrative and context. Viral outrage over "missing" features ended up distracting from these actually controversial mechanics that were cut from the game.

Some Missing Features Turned Out to be Ragebait Hoaxes


Plane Crash Animations Do Exist


Users criticized GTA 6's infamous 13 years of development for the lack of realism in clips showing planes bouncing off buildings upon impact with no explosion animations.
A community note later clarified that the absence of realistic explosions in these clips was due to the activation of the Reduced Vehicle Damage setting. This sparked debate among fans, with some accusing others of ragebaiting for clicks.
We personally crashed a plane into a building with Reduced Vehicle Damage turned off and confirmed that realistic impact animations do exist in GTA 6.

There Are No Gay Bars in Leonida


A number of players also complained about the inability to attack people inside a gay bar with a clip of Jason inside The Vault shooting at invincible NPCs. This claim has been debunked with players’ confirmation that there are no specifically gay or LGBTQ bars or clubs in GTA 6.
Other players also came forward to clarify that Rockstar isn’t unrealistically limiting player choice by protecting certain groups from in-game violence, but that weapons are simply deactivated inside certain venues like The Vault and all strip clubs, just as they were in GTA 5.
GTA 5 disables weapons inside strip clubs, but exploiting a glitch allows players to attack NPCs in strip clubs anyway by shooting before entering the establishment. GTA 6 patches this glitch by keeping strip club doors locked when you have a weapon equipped. But it’s open season for most outdoor bars, quayside bars, and dive bars, aligning with the game’s narrative focus on robbery, with Jason and Lucia starting as small-time criminals.

Our Take on Story v. Agency


Discourse was inevitable with a game of this magnitude. Some of the early backlash towards GTA 6's unrealistic graphics and gameplay has been attributed to sensationalized commentary aimed at capitalizing on the game's massive popularity.
But beyond the noise of launch-week ragebait lies substantive community debate about the friction between unprecedented hyperrealism in a massive open-world action RPG and limited player agency in service of its story.
Sources:
GTA 6 Famitsu Interview
GTA 6 Development Notes

item.title: GTA 6 Earns Eight Game Awards Nominations, but Jason’s Actor Misses Out
item.description:
GTA 6 earns eight Game Awards nominations, but Jason's Dylan Rourke misses out as Lucia's Manni L. Perez makes the shortlist. Find out what other categories GTA 6 has been nominated for and what fans think of Jason's performance.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 is Nominated for Eight Awards for The Game Awards 2026


Lucia Earns A Nomination for Her Performance


Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) has earned eight nominations at The Game Awards 2026, but Dylan Rourke, the actor behind Jason Duval, has missed out on Best Performance, as announced on November 17. Meanwhile, Manni L. Perez, who plays fellow protagonist Lucia Caminos, is the game’s only nominee in the acting category. She is joined by Angela Sant’Albano for Resident Evil Requiem, Liam McIntyre for Marvel’s Wolverine, Patrick Gibson for 007 First Light and Rahul Kohli for Saros.
Multiple performers from one game have made the shortlist before, since there’s no precedent for allowing only one actor from each game. Last year, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 earned three Best Performance nominations, with Ben Starr as Verso, Charlie Cox as Gustave, and Jennifer English as Maelle all in contention, with English eventually taking home the award.

Rockstar Last Won Four Awards in TGA 2018


GTA 6’s other nominations include Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, and Best Art Direction. Rockstar’s game is also competing for Best Score & Music, Best Audio Design, and Best Action/Adventure, alongside Perez’s acting nomination.
Back in 2018, Roger Clark won Best Performance for playing Arthur Morgan in Red Dead Redemption 2 (RDR2). Additionally, RDR2 won Best Narrative, Best Score/Music, and Best Audio Design, but lost Game of the Year to God of War.

Jason’s Reserved Personality Divides GTA 6 Fans


Reception Calls Jason's Performance Bland and Monotone


Jason’s Dylan Rourke missing out on his nomination is hardly surprising to fans, as early concerns have pointed out that he hasn’t made the same strong impression as Lucia in early previews. Now that the reviews are out and the game has officially been released, more players report that Jason’s reserved personality is his final iteration. In online forums, fans have said the character and his performance feel bland and monotone, lacking the energy expected of a GTA protagonist, especially compared to his fiery co-star Lucia and past protagonists like GTA 4’s Niko Bellic and GTA 5’s Michael De Santa.
Other fans argue that the opening hours offer a partial view of his character, and that he could improve alongside the narrative. Additionally, defenders think a more reserved lead is the perfect contrast to the outspoken people around him and the outrageous events usually expected of a GTA game.
In our review, we found that Jason’s laid-back personality complements Lucia, but his fierce loyalty has him feeling less developed on his own. It doesn’t help that his solo missions offer less insight into his personal motivations, which are mostly work-related, while Lucia gets to flesh out her character and the relationships around her outside of Jason. Aside from select interactions, Jason’s demeanor remains the same throughout the game, even delivering the same cadence during emotionally intense scenes.
The Game Awards takes place on December 10 in Los Angeles, with Rockstar’s latest competing across eight categories. Players can now judge Jason’s performance for themselves as they explore GTA 6’s story, with the game out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with a PC version to follow on an unannounced date.
Source:
The Game Awards 2026 Categories

item.title: GTA 6 Defies the Open World Checklist Template with Unmapped Encounters and Hidden Content
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI skips rigid map checklists for unscripted moments and hidden secrets in Vice City. Read on to learn more about its unmapped encounters, hidden content layers, and other details.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Skips Open-World Checklists for Unmapped Encounters and Hidden Secrets


Unmapped Encounters in Vice City and Hidden Secrets Beyond 100% Completion


Grand Theft Auto VI pushes back against the open-world habit of telegraphing side activities with map icons or clear prompts, letting unexpected scenes play out right in front of you across Vice City without spelling out what you're supposed to do. Many open-world titles turn exploration into a series of boxes to tick off, whereas this approach leans into organic moments as you explore the open world.
Instead of handing you a set objective with a marker, the game lets chaotic, reactive situations unfold naturally around traffic, NPC behavior, satire, and player choice. In the opening of his Bloomberg review, gaming reporter and author Jason Schreier highlighted an unmapped Vice City encounter involving a Sahara delivery truck (the game's parody of Amazon) and a fiery sedan crash that escalated into a wild lawsuit scheme, a BuckMe payout offer (the game's Venmo parody), and even a moment where he weighed blackmailing the guy.
Moments like that stand out because they let you react to a chain of events as they happen rather than following a scripted checklist. You do not need a prompt telling you an activity has started when the world itself sets off something unpredictable and funny on the fly.

How Hidden Discoveries Work Outside the 100% Checklist


That same design mindset shows up in how Grand Theft Auto 6 handles deeper secrets. While there is an extended list of content beyond the main story that counts toward the 100% completion achievement, Senior Design Director for Exploration & Ambient Content Ghyan Koehne noted in a Q&A for our GTA 6 review that extra layers of hidden content sit outside that 100% requirement.
"The world is filled with layers of slightly more hidden content," Koehne said, explaining that these unique pieces vary in scope and complexity. Some sit in a single spot waiting for observant players, while others only show up at night or when you return to an area later. Some tell a quick one-and-done story on a single visit, others change over multiple visits spaced out across days, and some point you toward a trail across multiple locations and encounters.
Besides timing and pacing, Koehne noted that some of these discoveries involve interacting with unique peds, including notable characters like Mandy, while others come from interacting with the environment itself. That mirrors how Red Dead Redemption 2 handles certain unmarked mysteries, like the "American Dreams" serial killer trail, where stumbling onto grisly murder scenes and collecting partial map pieces leads you to the killer's hideout without a quest marker handing you the lead from the start.
By blurring the lines between different kinds of world content and keeping some discoveries off the standard 100% checklist, Grand Theft Auto VI aims to keep Vice City feeling alive and surprising well past launch.
Sources:
Bloomberg GTA 6 Review

item.title: GTA 6 Has “A Lot More Than Two” Endings, Rockstar Confirms
item.description:
GTA 6 ends differently depending on how the game’s been played, with the campaign having more than two conclusions tied to player choices. Read on to learn about the factors that affect the story and more.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Has Multiple Endings Depending On Various Factors


Lucia and Jason's Fate Rests in The Player's Hands


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) trades the classic "choose your ending" option in prior titles for a different approach, where the way you play shapes how the story concludes. According to our Q&A with Rockstar, the campaign has "a lot more than two" possible endings, and the team does not consider any of them "bad."
The team went to great lengths to make sure every player's story is properly closed out. "We also don't think any ending is bad! They are just different conclusions based on the choices you made during the story," the team confirmed. Apart from making major choices that have consequences, the game still takes into account other aspects affecting the two main characters.
That makes it a clear break from earlier entries. GTA 4 asked players to choose between Deal and Revenge, and GTA 5 presented three options on a final mission menu. Iconic as they are, those moments often carried weight towards the ending versus the hours spent leading up to them.

Rockstar Says These Factors Affect The Outcome


According to Rockstar, four factors shape how GTA 6 wraps up:
  • Narrative Choices: Key decisions made across the story, such as whether you spare or eliminate certain characters during missions.

  • Lucia and Jason's Relationship: Whether the pair grow into a committed couple or stay strictly partners in crime. Rockstar explained in the development notes that "believable progression based on their overall investment in the relationship” determines their interactions.

  • Criminal Profile: How recklessly or cleanly you operated across Leonida, tracked across five reputation levels: Professional (beginner), Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable.

  • Family Savings Account: How much money you set aside for the duo's fresh start vs. spending it all along the way.

Rockstar also dropped a breadcrumb about one of the pair's closest associates: "Cal is out there with the hard drive, so who knows what will happen!" The remark suggests that Cal Hampton remains a loose thread, and that his fate, along with that of other characters, could feed into how things end. All other unknowns help add into the replayability of the game.
While the series is known for chaos, the latest entry rewards paying close attention to details such as bank balance, public or private conduct with other characters, and more. GTA 6 is now live on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

item.title: GTA 6 Makes Texting and Driving So Brutal It Might Actually Save Lives IRL
item.description:
GTA 6’s texting-while-driving mechanic is so difficult that it might discourage players from picking up their phones behind the wheel. Here is how the new feature doubles as a real-world road safety lesson, and what fans are saying about it.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Texting While Driving Mechanics Are a Nightmare


Could Teach Millions of Players Not to Text and Drive


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) features a somewhat realistic portrayal of texting while driving, which could actually benefit viewers in real life. For a franchise known for cultural satire and tackling controversial themes of violence and crime, the popular open-world action-adventure title may teach people a thing or two about keeping their eyes on the road.
According to a November 19, 2026 post on X (Twitter) by Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier, GTA 6 makes driving controls significantly harder when players use their in-game phones, which could discourage people from doing so in real life. “Grand Theft Auto VI could legitimately teach an entire generation not to text while driving, saving millions of lives,” he stated.
Schreier’s post includes a reposted clip showing a player driving one-handed along a beach while looking at their phone and brutally mowing down beachgoers in the process.
Some fans compared the mechanic to the drunk-driving feature in previous GTA titles, where driving under the influence blurs the player's vision and makes steering more difficult. Others jokingly noted that developer Rockstar Games has now done more for road safety than actual driver’s education programs.
There is a certain irony in GTA 6 potentially saving lives by discouraging distracted driving, all while letting players commit virtual murder and mayhem on the very same screen. To know more about our thoughts on Grand Theft Auto 6, check out our review below.
Source:
Jason Schreier X post on Texting and Driving in GTA 6

Wuthering Waves Version 4.0 To Welcome Seven New Characters


Seven Characters, with Lucia Expy Gordia


Wuthering Waves's newest 2D animated trailer, “Beneath Promeus’s Embrace,” revealed the seven new characters slated for release in the upcoming major chapter. While the character Anna was already revealed earlier on in Version 3.8, she will now debut as a playable Resonator sometime in the future. The following characters will also make their appearances in the game throughout 4.X, each with their own unique cryptic phrase that appears to hint at their future roles in the narrative:
 Anna - Roses and Desires
 April - Truth and Illusion
 Cairn - Blood Debts and Purifying Rain
 Gordia - Silent and Honed
 IYA - UFOs and Sparkles
 Lucielle - Future & Falsehoods
 Simulsys - Bones and Bygones

The official visuals for the new Resonators are now available on Wuthering Waves’ official social media channels. One character in particular has caught the eye of some eagle-eyed fans: Gordia’s design suggests that she is an expy (a character from a developer or franchise’s previous title appearing in another, like an Easter Egg) of Punishing Gray Raven’s (PGR) Lucia. Cairn also is visually similar to PGR’s Watanabe.

“Beneath Promeus’s Embrace” Trailer Reveals More of the New Federation


Wuthering Waves also revealed the upcoming location and the title of the newest major chapter. Through the animated trailer, players get to see the new stop in Rover’s journey for the first time: New Federation, a Western-inspired location. Each of the seven new Resonators appear in the trailer, presenting different facets of the new city through their eyes.

Chapter of the Year: Embers of the Everbright


One notable new addition to the update is the concept of the “Chapter of the Year.” Wuthering Waves normally plays its story out through episodic storylines centered around one version, but this time, it will present a “unified arc spanning a full year of in-depth storytelling.”
The development team has “strong confidence in its content volume, narrative quality, and long-term update cadence” for this upcoming season, and hopes that players will look forward to its story from its beginnings and throughout 2027.

item.title: Wuthering Waves’ 4.0 Announcement Teases What Looks to Be Another Lucia Expy
item.description:
Wuthering Waves Version 4.0 introduces Gordia, a character who bears a striking resemblance to Punishing: Gray Raven's Lucia. Read on to see our reaction to this character’s design and what it could mean for the game going forward.

Wuthering Waves’ 4.0 Announcement Teases What Looks to Be Another Lucia Expy


Lucia is Punishing: Gray Raven’s most recognizable character. Apologies to all the Alpha mains (myself included), Karenina fans, Vera worshippers, and Nanami enjoyers out there, but Lucia isn’t the game’s mascot for nothing.
That’s what makes Gordia, recently revealed through Wuthering Waves’ 4.0 Announcement (technically), so striking. At first glance, she looks like PGR’s most beloved character if she had a whip and a mean streak: the more visually blatant Lucia expy that many fans have been looking forward to for a long time.
Now, what exactly is an “expy”? While there’s no universally agreed-upon threshold for what constitutes one, the term itself is generally understood as shorthand for “exported character.” For the purposes of this article, we can generally categorize them into three kinds: Visual, Narrative, and Conceptual expys. Characters from HoYoverse-developed gacha games, in particular, provide plenty of examples of these categories, often with considerable overlap.
Yae Miko of Genshin Impact, for example, is primarily a visual expy of Yae Sakura from Honkai Impact 3rd, sharing recognizable design elements such as their long pink hair and fox motifs without necessarily sharing much of their character identities. An example of a conceptual expy, on the other hand, is Genshin Impact’s Raiden Shogun, who shares several conceptual and thematic elements with Raiden Mei, most notably their naming, lightning associations, and Kaminari-inspired imagery.
Wuthering Waves itself has had its fair share of expy comparisons, albeit with varying degrees of speculative backing. These range from the thematic and character-based similarities between Luna from PGR and Phrolova from WuWa, to the more visually oriented comparisons between Vera and Lupa/Yinlin. Not all of these comparisons are equally convincing, of course, but they demonstrate Kuro Games’ tendency and willingness to carry elements of its older character designs and concepts into its newer projects.

Recycling is Good if the Connections are Unique


Without knowing much about Gordia, all we can really assume is that she’s limited to being a visual expy of Punishing: Gray Raven’s Lucia. But why does that matter in the first place?
Well, we essentially already have a Lucia expy in Yangyang. She’s partly a visual one, but leans much more heavily to the narrative side as one of the protagonist’s earliest companions, having particularly strong protective streaks, being a constant source of belongingness, and so on.
Technically, however, you can imagine her as more of a homage-type character, as she shares traits with other members of the Gray Ravens like Lee and Liv.
Then, there’s also the “Mysterious Woman” who appears during the opening cutscene of the game, who also bears a striking resemblance to Lucia.
It matters because there will inevitably be identity-based conflict regarding these characters, especially if Kuro Games does follow up on its narrative promise of involving Yangyang more. While this may not be a concern for those who haven't touched Punishing: Gray Raven at all, players familiar with both games might find themselves comparing these characters against one another, particularly if they begin occupying similar narrative roles.
Of course, this isn't necessarily a bad thing. Characters can share inspirations without necessarily sharing identities. In fact, that's arguably the entire appeal of expys in the first place: taking recognizable elements from an existing character and reinterpreting them in a different setting. The important thing is ensuring that these characters have enough of their own identity to stand independently.
Yangyang, for instance, has her own history, motivations, and relationship with the Rover. Her similarities to Lucia don't invalidate those qualities, nor should they. The same should apply to Gordia. If anything, her introduction presents Kuro with another opportunity to demonstrate just how much mileage it can get out of an established and beloved character concept without simply reproducing the original. And if they can even provide a strong contrast from what players would expect from something designed similarly to their old character, then that's even better.
And maybe eventually, we’d get an actual Nanami expy that isn’t just a character (with lots of potential) swinging a chainsaw around—

item.title: GTA 6 Might Just Sweep The Game Awards 2026, Fans Say
item.description:
GTA 6's launch trailer arrives, and its release date lands just inside The Game Awards 2026 eligibility window. Read on to learn more about the timeline, rules, and other details.

GTA 6 Gears Up for Release and Makes It to The Game Awards 2026 Cutoff


Launch Trailer Arrives as TGA 2026 Eligibility Rules Surface


Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) revealed its official launch trailer on Rockstar Games’ X (Twitter), with a launch timeline that community members noted makes it eligible for The Game Awards 2026. The upbeat trailer introduces a new track, "Flower in a Hurricane," featuring prominent artists like Justice, Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. Many welcomed the video with hype, with comments praising both the cinematic snippets and the new track.
According to The Game Awards' FAQ, a title must be commercially available by Friday, November 20, at 9 PM (PT) to qualify for the 2026 ceremony. GTA 6 beats that deadline by just one day, releasing on November 19, 2026 after a series of delays. GTA 6 is also eligible for the Players' Voice category, which accepts entries until November 30, 2026. The ceremony itself will take place on December 10, 2026, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.

Cutoff Follows Past Years, Not a Special Exception


Multiple viral posts claimed the show made room specifically for Rockstar's game, but an X Community Note highlighted that the November 20 cutoff mirrors previous years. It is verified that past deadlines include November 21 for 2025 and November 22 for 2024, placing GTA 6 fairly within the standard window to be qualified.
Additionally, eligibility is only the first step, as the FAQ notes that nominees in most categories are selected by an international jury of over 100 media and influencer outlets. The jury decides winners by a vote split between the jury (90%) and public fan voting (10%). To give later entries a chance, publishers can also provide review copies or pre-release access to help outlets meet the balloting deadlines.

Split Over Whether GTA 6 Will Sweep


Reactions to the news have been fairly mixed. Some fans predict GTA 6 will dominate the show, with a few joking that other 2026 releases won’t stand a chance. Others within the gaming community expressed frustration, arguing that the title could simply win on hype alone before players can put in enough hours to evaluate the gameplay fairly.
However, many still defend its placement in the lineup. One fan argues that GTA 6 is a legitimate 2026 release qualifying within the standard period and that losing to another 2026 title would take nothing away from a strong year for gaming. Fan votes also represent only a small portion of the final score, and the jury still holds the majority of the weight in deciding the wins.
Given the scale of GTA 6’s release, it goes without saying that other publishers have reconsidered changing up their games’ release dates. A few noteworthy titles, like Danganronpa 2x2 and Fable, are already suspected to have been affected, so it’s no surprise that Rockstar’s hit series has shaken up the gaming industry’s timeline. item.title: GTA 6 Extended Look Hypes Fans For Release With 26 Minutes of New Gameplay
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI has received a new gameplay showcase following its previously announced Netflix premiere. Learn more about the new gameplay mechanics, world details, and community reactions.

Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look


New Look at the Gameplay, Map Exploration, and Mechanics


Grand Theft Auto VI developer and publisher Rockstar Games has officially released an extensive gameplay showcase. Launching as a timed exclusive on Netflix, the 26-minute presentation captured entirely on PlayStation 5 gave fans their very first deep dive into actual gameplay mechanics, missions, and open-world activities across the state of Leonida.
The showcase opens with a high-stakes mission featuring dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, highlighting a dynamic cover system, cooperative character AI, and seamless switching mechanics reminiscent of Grand Theft Auto V. Throughout the video, players are treated to a massive assortment of open-world recreational activities—including scuba diving, jet skiing, kayaking, dirt biking, base jumping, street racing, club dancing, and visiting strip clubs.

Detailed Police Tracking, Mission Variety, and Relationship Mechanics


The gameplay footage confirmed several heavily requested features and systemic upgrades coming to the game. Alongside the return of the iconic six-star wanted level system, the game introduces a sophisticated police tracking mechanism featuring on-screen HUD identification icons. The police now actively track specific evidence such as your physical description, your vehicle, and your current clothing. To successfully shake the authorities, players must use tactical strategies like switching out getaway vehicles, changing clothes, or ditching hot cars so the police lose their specific tracking data.
Missions and open-world progression offer distinct new structural depths, with certain high-stakes assignments giving players multiple tactical approaches, flexible escape routes, or specific job splits where tasks can only be taken by one of the dual protagonists. Complementing these mission structures, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained in an IGN interview that the game introduces a deeply integrated relationship system built around player choice. According to Nelson, players can choose how they want to handle Jason and Lucia's bond—whether that means nurturing their connection through shared moments like holding hands after leaving a store or opting out of the romantic side entirely without penalty. As Nelson noted, "Don’t bother with it if you aren’t. Up to you," clarifying that while the characters will always stay together as partners in crime for the narrative, extra relationship-building activities (like waiting for the other to get dressed, hanging out, or responding to texts) are entirely optional.
Additionally, players can interact with NPCs using a prompt system similar to Red Dead Redemption 2, pet or scold dogs to build karma, and manage various downtime activities like working out at gyms or watching satirical TV advertisements inside safehouses. The presentation also detailed complex melee combat, unique individual mission paths for Jason and Lucia, and intricate vehicle-entering mechanics.

Developer Insights on Immersion and Real-World Scale


Reflecting on the massive creative undertaking behind the project, The New York Times detailed how Rockstar approached the game's unprecedented fidelity and scale. Art director Aaron Garbut emphasized the studio's rigorous, hands-on approach to crafting the world, noting that instead of relying on procedural generation, developers art-directed non-player characters individually and packed rooms with bespoke details—from the tattoos on an NPC's arms to the specific drinks on a table.
Furthermore, developer Rob Nelson discussed the monumental technical challenge of bridging cinematic narrative and player freedom seamlessly. Comparing the studio's ambitions to a "moonshot," Nelson pointed out that allowing players to transition organically from daily safehouse routines like eating an apple or working out to high-stakes robberies and high-speed chases required completely reimagining how open-world systems interact. Rather than cutting away with black screens, the goal is to make every moment—whether on a mission or just exploring the swamps on an airboat—feel entirely continuous and transformative.

Netflix Streaming and Fans' Reactions


The Netflix showcase rollout successfully brought millions of viewers to the platform to catch the deep dive. The massive influx of eager fans tuning in all at once caused a temporary crash on Netflix, greeting users with error messages until access was restored.
The footage sparked an immediate wildfire of discussions across social media. Fans expressed overwhelming excitement over the gorgeous lighting, intricate physics, organic character banter, and relationship-shaping player choices like rushing Lucia's wardrobe changes, while internet forums heavily buzzed over details like the new evidence-based wanted icons, the return of the six-star system, and the depth of the game's open-world activities. With anticipation at an all-time high, Grand Theft Auto VI continues to cement its status as a once-in-a-generation cultural milestone ahead of its November release.

item.title: Arcane’s Sevika Was Pitched as a Wild Rift Champion, According to a Former Riot Developer
item.description:
Arcane's Sevika was pitched to debut as a Wild Rift champion but was overruled, according to a former Riot developer. Find out more details about the rejected pitch below.

Arcane’s Sevika Could Have Debuted as a Wild Rift Champion


A Former Riot Developer Says Her Sevika Pitch Was Overruled


Sevika from Arcane could have debuted as a Wild Rift champion, bringing Silco’s former lieutenant to the mobile version of League of Legends. Maddy Marquissee, the game’s former Champions Product Lead, said she "tried so hard" to make it happen and pitched Sevika for the roster but was ultimately overruled. Marquissee shared the detail on X (Twitter) on November 9 while responding to a fan who posted Sevika’s fight with the chem-baron Smeech from Arcane Season 2.
Fans in the thread were gutted that Sevika never made it onto the Wild Rift roster. Some felt she should have been given the same treatment as Ambessa and Mel Medarda, who both made the move from Arcane to both versions of LoL. One fan did ask Marquissee why the pitch had been overruled, and that question simply wasn't answered in the public thread.
Marquissee began working on Wild Rift while it was still in preproduction, helping develop tutorials and other features for new players. She later led the champions team and spoke publicly about Riot’s process for bringing Gwen over from PC League and reworking Karma for mobile, including a new ultimate. After leaving Riot, she now works at Wizards of the Coast as a principal product designer on Magic: The Gathering’s Secret Lair.
Norra, a portal-hopping yordle who arrived in February 2026, became the first champion to debut in Wild Rift and remains exclusive to its mobile roster. Players had already met her in Riot’s card game, Legends of Runeterra, and in Teamfight Tactics, where she shared a unit with her magical cat, Yuumi. In a follow-up thread, Marquissee called Norra "a great choice" and said the Wild Rift team killed it with their implementation.

Riot Has Already Experimented With a Playable Sevika


Sevika’s TFT Kit Ran on a Slot Machine


Fans have already seen how Sevika's lucky prosthetic arm would work in a game as TFT, where the kit was built around random attacks and random rewards. Sevika was one of the rarer recruits at launch in the League of Legends strategy spin-off, joining Into the Arcane as a 5 cost unit in November 2024.
Every time Sevika cast Beat the Odds her arm could produce a flamethrower, an extendable punch, or a chomp that would finish off a weakened enemy. A rare jackpot could yield gold or even a treasure chest. Her unique High Roller trait also gave her an extra roll for bonuses such as rockets, a shield, or more gold.
She and Smeech also shared the Chem-Baron trait where fielding enough Chem-Barons earned players Shimmer after fights, with bigger payouts during a losing streak. Players could then cash that Shimmer in for black-market gear. In a Riot post-set retrospective published on March 10, 2025, Riot Mort described Sevika and Smeech as "instant favorites." The article singled them out as two of the roster’s biggest successes, while other Arcane additions, including the enforcers Loris and Steb, struggled to generate the same enthusiasm.
Sevika is still one of the fan favorites in Arcane, and Riot could still very much bring her over to either version of League in the future. However, Arcane is over though and Riot are now looking at other stories across Runeterra. At the same time, 2XKO, a fighting game that seemed tailor-made for a brawler like Sevika, is winding down active development without her.
With the focus seems to be moving away from Piltover and Zaun, Marquissee's failed pitch at least gives us a taster of where the Wild Rift Sevika might have ended up.
